title: Cambridge IELTS 18 - Listening Test 1

sections.title: Section 1: Transport survey
sections.transcript:
[00:00] MAN: Excuse me. Would you mind if I asked you some questions? We're doing a survey on transport.
[00:08] SADIE: Yes, that's OK.
[00:11] MAN: First of all, can I take your name?
[00:14] SADIE: Yes. It's Sadie Jones.
[00:18] MAN: Thanks very much. And could I have your date of birth – just the year will do, actually. Is that all right?
[00:26] SADIE: Yes, that's fine. It's 1991.
[00:31] MAN: So next your postcode, please.
[00:34] SADIE: It's DW3Q 7YZ. [Q1]
[00:39] MAN: Great. Thanks. Is that in Wells?
[00:43] SADIE: No, it's actually in Harborne – Wells isn't far from there, though.
[00:50] MAN: I really like that area. My grandmother lived there when I was a kid.
[00:56] SADIE: Yes, it is nice.
[01:00] MAN: Right, so now I want to ask you some questions about how you travelled here today. Did you use public transport?
[01:09] SADIE: Yes. I came by bus.
[01:13] MAN: OK. And that was today. It's the 24th of April, isn't it? [Q2]
[01:20] SADIE: Isn't it the 25th? No, actually, you're right.
[01:26] MAN: Ha ha. And what was the reason for your trip today? I can see you've got some shopping with you.
[01:34] SADIE: Yes. I did some shopping but the main reason I came here was to go to the dentist. [Q3]
[01:43] MAN: That's not much fun. Hope it was nothing serious.
[01:48] SADIE: No, it was just a check-up. It's fine.
[01:52] MAN: Good. Do you normally travel by bus into the city centre?
[01:58] SADIE: Yes. I stopped driving in ages ago because parking was so difficult to find and it costs so much. [Q4]
[02:08] MAN: I see.
[02:10] SADIE: The bus is much more convenient too. It only takes about 30 minutes.
[02:17] MAN: That's good. So where did you start your journey?
[02:22] SADIE: At the bus stop on Claxby Street. [Q5]
[02:27] MAN: Is that C-L-A-X-B-Y?
[02:30] SADIE: That's right.
[02:35] MAN: And how satisfied with the service are you? Do you have any complaints?
[02:42] SADIE: Well, as I said, it's very convenient and quick when it's on time, but this morning it was late. Only about 10 minutes, but still. [Q6]
[02:55] MAN: Yes, I understand that's annoying. And what about the timetable? Do you have any comments about that?
[03:03] SADIE: Mmm. I suppose I mainly use the bus during the day, but any time I've been in town in the evening – for dinner or at the cinema – I've noticed you have to wait a long time for a bus – there aren't that many. [Q7]
[03:23] MAN: OK, thanks. So now I'd like to ask you about your car use.
[03:29] SADIE: Well, I have got a car but I don't use it that often. Mainly just to go to the supermarket. But that's about it really. My husband uses it at the weekends to go to the golf club. [Q8]
[03:48] MAN: And what about a bicycle?
[03:51] SADIE: I don't actually have one at the moment.
[03:55] MAN: What about the city bikes you can rent? Do you ever use those?
[04:01] SADIE: No – I'm not keen on cycling there because of all the pollution. But I would like to get a bike – it would be good to use it to get to work. [Q9]
[04:17] MAN: So why haven't you got one now?
[04:20] SADIE: Well, I live in a flat – on the second floor and it doesn't have any storage – so we'd have to leave it in the hall outside the flat. [Q10]
[04:34] MAN: I see. OK. Well, I think that's all …

sections.title: Section 2: Becoming a volunteer for ACE
sections.transcript:
[00:02] Speaker: Good evening everyone, and welcome to this introductory session on volunteering for ACE.
[00:10] First, my apologies about the seating arrangements tonight. Some of the seats are placed very close together, which isn't ideal.
[00:25] Now, people often ask about our age requirements. The age of volunteers is really less important than other factors like reliability and enthusiasm.
[00:42] Regarding training: we ensure it is continuous throughout your journey with us.
[01:00] Before applying, please consider two key issues: your level of commitment and your availability during weekends.
[01:25] Let me outline the various roles: For fundraising, original and new ideas are particularly welcome.
[01:45] For litter collection, volunteers need a good level of fitness.
[02:05] For 'Playmates', our nutrition program, an understanding of food and diet is essential.
[02:25] In our Story club, having experience on stage helps captivate young audiences.
[02:45] And for first aid duties, having a good memory for emergency procedures is vital.

sections.title: Section 3: Talk on jobs in fashion design
sections.transcript:
[00:05] Hugo: Hi Chantal, how did you find the guest lecture on fashion industry careers?
[00:12] Chantal: Well, at the beginning I struggled because the students sitting next to me were talking loudly.
[00:24] Hugo: Same here! But what surprised both of us was that there is much more variety in the job market than we had realised.
[00:40] Chantal: Absolutely. Though we both agreed the speaker's main message was quite hard for us to follow at points.
[00:55] Hugo: And our school careers advice was delivered far too late in the academic year.
[01:10] Chantal: When looking to our own futures, you and I differ on why we would like a career in fashion.
[01:28] Hugo: Regarding unpaid internships: I feel realistic about the practice – it's just the norm.
[01:45] Chantal: The speaker admitted two early mistakes: paying too much attention to how she looked, and expecting to become well known right away.
[02:10] Hugo: We also found two valuable retail statistics: the reasons why people return items, and the fashion designs customers want but can't find.

sections.title: Section 4: Elephant translocation
sections.transcript:
[00:05] Lecturer: Today we examine the large-scale elephant translocation from Majete National Park.
[00:18] Overpopulation caused intense competition and extensive damage to fences in the reserve.
[00:32] In the translocation, an entire family unit was selected to keep social structures intact.
[00:48] Vets and park rangers employed helicopters to herd the animals towards open plains.
[01:05] Tranquilising had to be swift to minimise physiological stress.
[01:20] Elephants were carefully positioned on their sides to prevent their immense weight from crushing their lungs.
[01:38] Their breathing was monitored constantly throughout transit.
[01:52] Scientists recorded biological data including tusk lengths and the circumference of their feet.
[02:10] At Nkhotakota Reserve, the project created valuable employment opportunities for local trackers.
[02:26] Heavy patrols caused a sharp decline in poachers and confiscated weapons.
[02:42] Ultimately, eco-tourism flourished, providing a significant boost to the national GDP.
